title: The Ternary Operator
objective: Write a one-line if/else using the ternary operator.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; the loop half of this book chapter is covered in Code Forge's Loops chapter. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: The ternary operator is a one-line shortcut for a simple if/else that produces a value instead of running separate blocks. The pattern is condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse, read almost like a sentence: if the condition holds, use this value, otherwise use that one.

Because a ternary expression evaluates to a single value, you can log it directly, store it in a variable, or use it anywhere else an if/else would otherwise force you to write several lines. let status = age >= 18 ? "adult" : "child"; does the same job as a four-line if/else.
Reach for a ternary when both outcomes are simple values and the choice itself is the whole point. If either branch needs more than one line of logic, a regular if/else is clearer.
explanation.rule: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse evaluates to one of two values in a single expression — a shortcut for a simple if/else, not a replacement for every one.

examples.title: Positive or Negative
examples.note: num > 0 is false, so result becomes 'negative' — the same outcome as a four-line if/else, in one line.

examples.title: Using It Directly in a console.log
examples.note: No variable needed — the ternary's result is passed straight into console.log().

checks.question: let num = 4; let result = num % 2 === 0 ? "even" : "odd"; — what is result?

feedback.correct: Correct — num % 2 === 0 is true for 4, so result becomes "even".
feedback.incorrect: Check the condition first: num % 2 === 0 is true whenever num is even.

assignment.title: Access Level
assignment.brief: Write accessLevel(role) that returns 'full access' if role is 'admin', otherwise 'limited access' — using the ternary operator, not an if statement.
requirements: Use the ternary operator (condition ? a : b) on the return line.
Do not use a separate if statement.

requirementChecks.label: Does not use an if statement

assignment.outputCheckLabel: accessLevel('admin') and accessLevel('guest') log full access then limited access

hints: The pattern is: return condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse.
No if statement is needed — this all fits on one return line.
accessLevel('guest') should return 'limited access' since 'guest' isn't 'admin'.
